title: Why Interactive Brokers Stock Tumbled on Tuesday
detail:
Why Interactive Brokers Stock Tumbled on Tuesday
Danny Vena, CPA, The Motley Fool
Tue, September 1, 2026 at 11:43 AM PDT 3 min read
NVDA
IBKR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Interactive Brokers Group (NASDAQ: IBKR) slipped on Tuesday, falling as much as 6.3%. As of 2:18 p.m. ET, the stock was still down 6%.

The catalyst that drove the brokerage and trading platform lower was bearish commentary by one of Wall Street's finest.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Fully baked?

UBS analyst Michael Brown downgraded Interactive Brokers to neutral (hold) from buy, though he increased his price target to $102, up from $50. That represents potential upside for investors of roughly 5% compared to Monday's closing price -- so he's clearly playing catch-up.

Brown appears to have mixed feelings about the stock. One the one hand, the analyst views Interactive Brokers as "a best-in-class broker with a compelling growth runway." He expects the company to generate low-teens earnings per share (EPS) growth over the coming five years, fueled by account and client asset growth and increased trading activity. The analyst also called the platform "highly efficient," which will allow Interactive Brokers to maintain its gross margin in the high 70% range.

The analyst also cited a suite of new products -- including cryptocurrency, prediction markets, and advanced tools -- which he believes will deepen both customer engagement and wallet share.

So what's not to like? Brown says the current stock price "already reflects much of that advantage."

The analyst has a point. As of market close yesterday, Interactive Brokers stock was trading for nearly 39 times earnings and 36 times forward earnings. While that's not particularly egregious, the valuation is a bit stretched for a company expected to grow earnings by low double digits.

On the other hand, Interactive Brokers' stock is up 47% over the past year, well ahead of the 18% gains of the S&P 500. In fact, the stock has far outpaced the broader market over the past three and five years -- which helps illustrate why Interactive Brokers is deserving of a premium.

Chips are big business and make big headlines.

Globally, according to Fortune Business Insights, the semiconductor market was valued at $598.06 billion in 2025, and is expected to reach more than $1.47 trillion by 2034, representing a CAGR of 10.60% over the period.

The US holds a vital position in the chip industry. The American market, with its combination of design and innovation leadership in semiconductors, its advanced manufacturing capabilities, and its strong protections for intellectual property, is a natural host for strong chip companies and a high level of industry talent. And that makes American chip companies a natural target for investors. Nvidia, the world's largest chipmaker, is also the largest firm on Wall Street, with a market cap in excess of $5.2 trillion.

However, two of Wall Street's top-ranked analysts are saying that investors should look past the multi-trillion-dollar industry giants, and even look past the multi-hundred-billion-dollar rising stars – because there are small names worth buying. These are chip makers with double-digit-billion-dollar market cap values – but with potential to bring solid upside to the table.

We've opened up the database at TipRanks to get a good look at two names which are getting love from some 5-star analysts. Here's a closer look at them, to see just what's making them compelling choices today.

Lattice Semiconductor Corporation (LSCC)

First up on this list is Lattice Semiconductor, a firm that has built itself a sound niche in the industry by focusing on a specific role, mastering it, and riding it to consistent profitability. For Lattice, that role is in the design, production, and distribution of low-power and power-efficient field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). The company has over 40 years' experience, working at the leading edge of the semiconductor field, and has become the industry's leader in the supply of FPGAs.

These chips are used in a variety of applications, including control, secure connectivity, and power management in smart computing, mobile devices, industrial and automotive systems. FPGAs are also widely used in data centers; Lattice doesn't provide the headline-grabbing GPUs and CPUs, but its chips are used alongside these chips to handle power sequencing and protocol bridging. In addition, as data centers expand and their architecture evolves, Lattice is finding that demand for its products is also expanding.

title: Michael Burry's Biggest AI Bets Take Surprising Turn
detail:
Michael Burry's Biggest AI Bets Take Surprising Turn
Moz Farooque ACCA
Tue, September 1, 2026 at 11:01 AM PDT 2 min read
NVDA
MU
PLTR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio)'s contrarian portfolio took a beating in August as several of his biggest bearish AI bets moved sharply against him, led by Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR), Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU). The famed investor's positioning highlights a growing risk for AI bears: even when valuation concerns look extreme, momentum and earnings growth can keep expensive stocks climbing far longer than skeptics expect.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with PLTR.

Is PLTR fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Seven of the nine stocks Burry was bearish on advanced during August. Palantir was the biggest problem, surging more than 50% even as Burry maintained out-of-the-money put options extending into March 2027 with strike prices in the low-to-mid $100s.

Nvidia added another 10% during the month. Burry held bearish December 2026 and June 2027 puts while also owning higher-strike December calls, giving him some protection around Nvidia's earnings.

Micron created another headache. Burry had increased his short exposure after arguing that the memory maker's enormous rally reflected speculation more than fundamentals, yet MU shares gained 16.49% in August.

Other bearish positions also went the wrong way: CoreWeave rose 18%, Oracle gained 14.8%, Nebius advanced 8%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF added 1.22%.

His long book performed considerably better, although results were mixed. Veeva Systems (NYSE:VEEV) surged 40%, while Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) climbed 17%. Fannie Mae gained 5.7% and MercadoLibre added 3%.

But PayPal fell 8%, Sprouts Farmers Market lost 6%, and Flutter Entertainment dropped 4%. Burry also remains bullish on Lululemon, which he has described as screaming cheap, and has increased his exposure to JD.com after exiting Alibaba.

Investors Takeaway

August illustrates the difference between identifying valuation risk and successfully timing it. Burry may ultimately be right that parts of the AI trade are overpriced, but Palantir, Nvidia and Micron continue to enjoy powerful earnings and sentiment momentum.

Investors should therefore watch revenue growth, earnings revisions and valuation multiples rather than Burry's short positions alone. A meaningful slowdown in AI spending or weaker guidance could rapidly validate his thesis. Until then, his August performance shows why betting against a powerful growth cycle can be painful even when the valuation argument looks compelling.

Oracle Corp (NYSE: ORCL) stock is falling today, down 5.4% as of 1:52 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, as bond yields continue to rise, which could have serious consequences for the debt-laden tech giant.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite are both down, sliding 0.7% and 0.9%, respectively.

The 30-year Treasury yield is near a 20-year high

As U.S. 30-year treasury yields hover near 20-year highs, major bond markets around the world are setting their own records. In Japan, 10-year notes hit their highest level since 1996, while in the U.K., yields on the 30-year Gilt set a near 30-year record.

Bond markets are uneasy over persistent inflation and global conflicts, especially the Iran war, which has reignited in recent days. Oil prices are once again moving higher.

Oracle's free cash flow was negative $23.7 billion in fiscal 2026

This has consequences for businesses across the market, but Oracle is especially sensitive to changes in the bond market. That's because it is currently spending enormous sums in a race to build AI data centers as quickly as possible.

Image source: Getty Images.

And it's spending considerably more than it's taking in -- free cash flow (FCF) dropped to negative $23.7 billion last year. To fund the difference, Oracle raised $43 billion from the debt market last year and expects to raise another $20 billion in the current year, in addition to a $20 billion equity raise.

Rising yields mean borrowing becomes more expensive.

title: Ripe Brings Old School DeFi Farming to Robinhood Chain
detail:
Ripe Brings Old School DeFi Farming to Robinhood Chain
Bankless
Tue, September 1, 2026 at 12:04 PM PDT 3 min read
NVDA
AAPL
SPCX
GOOG
DEGEN30096-USD
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

In recent days, Robinhood Chain's metrics are up and to the right. Transactions, volume, revenue, deploys, you name it.

Helping this surge is a growing field of native apps like Pons, Index, and Stocknet, all of which can be, or are explicitly designed to be, used with the L2's blooming cast of tokenized stocks, e.g. NVDA, AAPL, SPCX, GOOGL, etc.

Among these, one particular project making big waves today is letting users put their Robinhood Chain ecosystem tokens (both app and stock tokens) to work in old school DeFi yield farms that are reminiscent of 2020's Yam Finance.

The project? Ripe Protocol. It's a classic degen opp, and early on, so tread cautiously if you do explore. But even if you don't, Ripe might revitalize Yam's "food farms" style again, so it's worth catching up on the basics in any case.

The Ripe 101

Ripe is a multi-collateral borrowing protocol.

Instead of siloed vaults per asset (i.e. the Maker model where 5 assets means 5 separate loans + 5 separate liquidation risks), Ripe is designed to let you deposit your whole portfolio, ETH, stablecoins, tokenized stocks, etc., and then borrow a single stablecoin, GREEN, against all of it at once.

Naturally, GREEN targets a $1 peg and burns on every repayment, while its yield-bearing version, sGREEN, auto-compounds protocol revenue for anyone who'd rather hold than actively manage a loan.

As for supported collateral types, Ripe currently accepts WETH plus the Robinhood-issued tokenized stocks NVDA, AAPL, SPCX, GOOGL, TSLA, and GME, each at a flat 70% loan-to-value and 7% borrow rate.

For example, you could deposit tokenized GME, borrow GREEN against it, and keep the stock's upside without selling. This is precisely the sort of programmable finance around stocks that Robinhood Chain was built for.

Digging into the farms

Along with the borrowing side of things, Ripe is currently running RIPE token distributions across a set of protocol vaults and community farms, i.e. traditional liquidity mining.

You can find these farms on Ripe's Earn page or alternatively, if you prefer a more nostalgic and detailed setup, through the new vfat.tools Ripe dashboard.

Many of the stated yields here are extremely juicy right now, but these APYs/APRs will fluctuate with the volatility of the RIPE price, so don't consider the rates you see as ironclad at any given time.

The farms themselves are divided into two categories, protocol vaults and community farms.

Per vfat, the RIPE/NVDA LP (a.k.a. UNI-V2) farm and the RIPE farm are the highest yielding protocol vaults at the moment, nominally offering ~23,669% APR and ~8,423% APR respectively at the time of writing.

title: Prediction: Palantir's Commercial Revenue Passes Its Government Revenue Before 2027, and the Stock's Growth Math Changes With It.
detail:
Prediction: Palantir's Commercial Revenue Passes Its Government Revenue Before 2027, and the Stock's Growth Math Changes With It.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Tue, September 1, 2026 at 11:57 AM PDT 6 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For most of its life, Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) has been a government software company.

Even now, with shares near $186 as of this writing, the artificial intelligence (AI) software specialist's biggest business at home is still the one built on government contracts. U.S. government revenue was $809 million in the second quarter, against $764 million for U.S. commercial.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But the gap is down to $45 million, and the two lines are not growing at the same speed. Last quarter, the U.S. commercial side grew 149% year over year. The government side grew 90%.

Roll those curves forward and they cross almost immediately. My prediction: U.S. commercial revenue passes U.S. government revenue in the third quarter of 2026 (the quarter that ends this month), and well before 2027 even if the timing slips.

That crossover would be more than a milestone, because when the faster-growing business becomes the bigger one, the whole company's growth rate starts bending toward it.

Image source: Getty Images.

Two lines, $45 million apart

The second quarter is the closest the race has been all year. U.S. commercial revenue reached $764 million, up 149% year over year and 28% from the first quarter. U.S. government revenue reached $809 million, up 90% year over year and 18% sequentially.

Both rates are extraordinary at this scale. The government side's 90% alone would be a standout result for most software companies. The commercial side has simply been faster, and consistently so. In the first quarter, the same race ran 133% against 84%.

Notably, though, the quarter-to-quarter race is tighter. In the first quarter, the government business grew faster sequentially, 21% versus 18%. That flip came from a customer program moving out of the commercial segment and into the government one. Management said commercial growth would have reached 143% year over year without the transition.

Still, the year-over-year gap is the durable pattern -- 49 percentage points in the first quarter, 59 in the second.

Management credits the surge to demand for what CEO Alex Karp calls "AI sovereignty," meaning customers want control over their own operations, data, and decisions.

When do the lines cross?

Take the second quarter's sequential rates and roll them one quarter forward. Commercial revenue growing 28% from $764 million lands at about $980 million. Government revenue growing 18% from $809 million lands at about $955 million. On that math, the lines cross in the third quarter, the period ending Sept. 30.
